# China's new five-year plan calls for AI throughout its economy, tech breakthroughs

Reuters, By Laurie Chen and Eduardo Baptista, March 5, 2026. (NOTE: Reuters page is paywalled; only the lede is directly readable. Key figures below corroborated from Reuters' own secondary coverage and the MarketScreener syndication of the same Reuters article.)

## Lede (directly readable)
BEIJING, March 5 (Reuters) - China's new five-year policy blueprint laid out its ambitions to aggressively adopt artificial intelligence throughout the world's second-biggest economy and dominate emerging technologies such as quantum computing and humanoid robots.

## Key facts (corroborated from Reuters / MarketScreener syndication, same article)
- The country will "seize the commanding heights of science and technological development" and seek "decisive breakthroughs in key core technologies", according to the plan released Thursday to coincide with the opening session of the National People's Congress.
- The 141-page five-year blueprint mentioned AI more than 50 times and included a sweeping "AI+ action plan".
- A separate report by the country's state-planning body (NDRC) asserted that China was outpacing rivals in AI research and development as well as other key areas.
- Specific measures: experimenting with robots to perform jobs in sectors suffering from labour shortages; deploying AI agents that can perform tasks with minimal human guidance; increase investment in quantum computing, 6G, embodied AI (humanoid robots), and machine-brain interfaces.
- The plan pledged "key breakthroughs in nuclear fusion technologies", a reusable heavy-load rocket, an integrated space-earth quantum communication network, scalable quantum computers, and a feasibility demonstration of a lunar research station.
- China aims to become a world leader in frontier R&D by "accelerating breakthroughs in basic theories and foundational technologies" and investing in basic research and cultivating a world-class STEM talent base.
- The government promised to build out "hyper-scale" computing clusters supported by cheap and abundant electricity and to support AI open-source communities.
- Growth target for the 2026-2030 period set at 4.5%-5% (per companion Reuters coverage, March 4-5, 2026).
- This is China's 15th five-year plan since adopting Soviet-style quinquennial planning in the 1950s.
